text_blocks.snippet: GST stands for Goods and Services Tax, a comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based indirect tax levied on the supply of goods and services. Introduced in India on July 1, 2017, it replaced a web of multiple overlapping central and state indirect taxes—such as VAT, service tax, central excise duty, and luxury tax—under a unified "one nation, one tax" framework.

list.snippet: Indirect Tax: It is collected by the seller at the point of sale and eventually borne by the end consumer.
Destination-Based: The tax revenue goes to the state where the goods or services are consumed rather than where they are produced.

Multi-Stage & Input Tax Credit (ITC): Tax is applied at every step of the supply chain. Businesses can claim credit for the GST they paid on raw materials or business expenses, ensuring tax is paid only on the value added at each stage (eliminating the "cascading" or tax-on-tax effect).
CGST (Central Goods and Services Tax): Levied by the Central Government on intra-state sales (within the same state).
SGST (State Goods and Services Tax): Levied by the State Government on intra-state sales.
IGST (Integrated Goods and Services Tax): Levied by the Central Government on inter-state (between two different states) sales and imports.
UGST (Union Territory Goods and Services Tax): Levied on transactions within Union Territories without a legislature.

text_blocks.snippet: Goods and services are categorized into different tax brackets—frequently including rates like 0%, 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%—depending on whether they are daily essentials, standard services, or luxury items.
You can read a detailed overview of compliance and rules on the CBIC GST Portal.
